A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Renumbered, relocated and merged material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original controlled training experiments, evaluations of Pythia and OLMo, post-training experiments, and appendix sensitivity and attention analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds an attention-head intervention experiment in Appendix H and Table 6.

M1.justification: V3 Appendix H adds an auxiliary inference procedure that scales identified in-context attention-head activations, following Yu et al. (2023). The core architecture, corpus-controlled training framework, pretraining objective and post-training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic biographies, real and synthetic country-capital tasks, and Tulu instruction tuning. The new head intervention uses the existing biography conflict setting. Legal and medical examples in v3 are discussion examples, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: Existing corpus-condition and before/after instruction-tuning comparisons retain their comparator sets. Appendix H varies activations within the study's models; it does not introduce a competing method benchmark.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces an intervention protocol using activation multipliers 0, 0.5, 1 and 2 on high-frequency entities, for Zipfian models trained with 0% or 1% noise. Existing evaluation metrics, sampling schedules, training budgets and sensitivity settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix H tests whether attention-head suppression or amplification changes conflict preferences and whether the response depends on training noise. Earlier attention analysis and entity-count, noise-level and distributional-skew sweeps remain; v2 Figures 15-17 become v3 Figure 15a-c.

E5.justification: Existing plot shading and regression annotations are retained. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions or significance tests; new Table 6 reports point estimates only.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds intervention results: increasing the activation multiplier from 1 to 2 changes in-context preference from 69.50% to 81.75% without noise and from 1.75% to 17.50% with 1% noise. These are new experimental results, not improvements over v2 scores. Retained numerical tables and result plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The accuracy/preference definitions and Zipf distribution formula remain unchanged. V3's note that the two preferences need not sum to one explains existing definitions; no new proof, theorem or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claim that repetition, moderate inconsistency and skewed knowledge frequency jointly enable balanced knowledge use, together with corresponding real-world training dynamics and adjustable post-training preferences. Rewording does not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 distinguishes synthetic causal evidence from real-world correlations and explicitly discusses small-model limitations, but removes v2's specific caveats about retrieval errors, partial relevance and multi-document conflicts. Section 4.2 adds deployment advice based on source reliability, while Appendix H interprets noisy-training preferences as resistant to inference interventions.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository pointer, specifies final pretraining checkpoints for the instruction-tuning comparison, and expands the LLM-use disclosure to experimental code development. It omits v2's explicit randomized attribute-order description. Architecture, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds Kim et al. (2026) and Lee et al. (2026), and removes Hoffmann et al. (2022). Appendix H explicitly positions training-data analysis as complementary to attention-head interventions. The central positioning as a controlled study of knowledge-use emergence remains.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, setup, experimental discussion, related work, conclusion and limitations. Section 4 becomes question-led Discussion and Implications, terminology is standardized, and appendix prose and subsection organization are revised. This is substantial editorial revision beyond the added experiment.

P2.justification: The dataset illustration moves from v2 Figure 9 in the appendix to v3 Figure 2 in the main text. Schematics are restyled, Table 5 is reorganized, Figures 15-17 are merged into Figure 15a-c, and Table 6 is added. Existing result plots retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V3 provides clearer exposition, a code-access pointer, a focused intervention study, and a more careful distinction between synthetic causal evidence and real-world correlation. These modest gains strengthen the paper without changing its main results. Benefits are tempered by limited head-selection details, removal of specific RAG limitations, and deployment extrapolations in Section 4.2 that neither PDF evaluates.
